runs.summary: The review assessed the Agreement against the DMCC rules on Company status, registration, Articles, licensing, Branches, names, continuation and corporate capacity. Most registration, Branch, name and continuation provisions are not applicable to this shareholders’ agreement, and the Company’s status and licensing obligations are generally addressed. The principal issue is that the licensing section omits the regulatory allocation of liabilities and commitments during pre-licence and suspended-licence periods. The review identified direct conflicts concerning bearer shares, share issuance currencies, capital reduction procedures, share transfers, and Director qualifications. The Agreement also omits the mandatory Registrar notification deadline for Director changes. Dividend provisions align with the stated distribution restrictions, while Holding Company, Subsidiary, cross-holding, class-rights, and Treasury Share provisions were not applicable on the stated facts. The review identified direct conflicts with mandatory DMCC requirements, including prohibited Director financial assistance, rejection of the Secretary requirement, non-compliant meeting rules, US GAAP accounting, an excessive first financial year and insufficient record retention. Manager, auditor, disqualification, inspection and regulatory-cooperation provisions are also incomplete. These issues should be aligned with the DMCCA Regulations and the Articles before reliance on the Agreement. The review identified partial treatment of voluntary winding-up, liquidation priority, liquidator qualifications, and licence suspension. The agreement omits or leaves unclear several mandatory DMCC procedures for insolvency reporting, solvent and insolvent winding-up, dissolution, and licence termination or strike-off. Amalgamation, sanctions, and statutory unfair-prejudice remedies are not contractual subjects addressed by this agreement. The review assessed the agreement against DMCC disclosure and voluntary licence suspension requirements. The disclosure clause is incomplete because it omits several mandatory reporting safeguards and the prohibitions concerning false or concealed information. findings.title: Bearer shares required

findings.title: Invalid capital reduction

findings.title: Incomplete transfer formalities

findings.title: Unqualified alternate directors
findings.description: The Agreement expressly permits an alternate director not to meet the director qualification requirements, contrary to the requirement that an alternate satisfy the applicable qualification criteria.

findings.title: Prohibited Director Assistance
findings.description: Clause 2.5 permits loans, guarantees, and other financial assistance to Directors. The Regulations prohibit a Company from providing financial assistance to a Director, regardless of shareholder approval or monetary limits. Clause 2.4 also does not cover all continuing duties relating to acts or omissions before cessation.

findings.title: Secretary Requirement Omitted
findings.description: The Agreement states that the Company is not required to appoint a Secretary. A DMCC Company must have a Secretary unless it is an SPV, and the document identifies the entity as a DMCC company without stating that it is an SPV.

findings.title: Manager Notice Deadline Missing

They also do not expressly require appointment by resolution of the Directors or address all statutory qualification and replacement requirements.

findings.title: Officer Disqualification Controls Missing

findings.title: General Meeting Rules Conflict

findings.title: Financial Reporting Conflicts
findings.description: The Agreement requires US GAAP instead of IFRS, makes the first financial year 24 months instead of no more than 18 months, and retains records for three years instead of at least five years. It also omits several required approval, audit, filing, and registered-office record provisions.

findings.title: Incomplete Solvency Process

findings.title: Incomplete Licence Enforcement Provisions

runs.summary: The review identified one material issue concerning the Agreement's unqualified statement of limited Shareholder liability. The licensing provisions are aligned with the listed DMCC requirements, while registration, Articles, Branch, name-change, continuation, and transfer-out provisions are not applicable to this shareholders' agreement. No additional issue was identified under the listed corporate-capacity clause. The review identified direct conflicts concerning bearer shares, capital reductions, share currencies, share transfers, and Director qualifications. The Agreement also omits mandatory company-register provisions and the required Registrar notification for Director changes. Dividend provisions align with the listed distribution requirements, while class-rights, Treasury Share, and subsidiary provisions are not applicable to the arrangements described. The review identified direct conflicts with DMCC requirements concerning Director financial assistance, the Company Secretary, Manager notifications, disqualification procedures and General Meetings. It also found material accounting, financial-year, record-retention and audit omissions or inconsistencies. The agreement does not restrict DMCCA inspection or compliance-direction powers. The review identified material omissions in the Agreement's winding-up, liquidation, insolvency, and licence-enforcement provisions. Section 11 partially addresses solvent winding-up and payment priority, but does not cover the full DMCC reporting, creditor, liquidator, dissolution, or insolvent-winding-up procedures. Section 9 addresses suspension only and omits the statutory termination and strike-off consequences. The review considered the agreement’s regulatory disclosure provisions and its treatment of DMCC licence suspension. The disclosure clause is incomplete and the bearer-transfer wording may hinder required regulatory disclosure. The suspension clause addresses cessation after suspension but does not provide enough detail to establish compliance with the voluntary-suspension process.
